main_body: Round leaf canopy (rows ~1-30) on a brown trunk with root flare (rows 30-46)
top_band: Canopy top: lighter green highlight clump at rows 1-10 blending into mid greens; no discrete flat top band, organic dome shading
evidence: The canopy is a rounded dome with a lit upper area (rows 1-10) that gives a top-lit volume, and a darker underside (rows 24-30) that works as shadow over the trunk. The trunk below has a lit left side and a shaded right side and flares into roots. For an organic object this reads as a 3/4 volume, not a flat elevation, and there is no isometric side face. It is a bit simple: the top is expressed by light gradation rather than a separate band.

style.evidence: The canopy has about 5 green steps with blocky clumps and a light highlight at the upper left, which is reasonable. Against the references it is smoother and more uniform: no individual leaf clusters, no branches visible inside the canopy, and no leaf-edge silhouette breakup. The outline is near-black on the canopy edge and the trunk base, with some dark green at the lower canopy, so it leans toward a sticker look. The trunk is a plain two-tone column with only a few dark grain dots, and the right half of the canopy is a large area of near-flat dark green. Overall it reads thinner and flatter than the Beodeul trees.
